tip: Starting a clause, Wie with no named person means whoever: Wie jarig is = whoever has a birthday.
Doen aan means to take part in or practice something: doen aan het poldermodel = go in for the polder model.
Genoeg goes after the adjective, not before it: dik genoeg = thick enough, never genoeg dik.
Waaien is a weather verb used with het: het waait = it is windy, just like het regent for it rains.
For an action still going on, Dutch uses the present with al: al dertig jaar zorgt = has been caring for thirty years.
